business_impact: Customer ticket-detail requests remain successful but experience materially elevated latency while CPU contention causes sustained throttling inside the API runtime.
reproduction: Deploy a normal APP-004 exercise release, establish the fixed 0.25-CPU API budget, and prove a healthy ticket-read latency baseline. Start the controlled OPSFORGE CPU-burn processes inside the existing API container without changing the image, release, main API process, or CPU budget. Repeated ticket-detail requests remain HTTP 200 but p95 latency increases, docker process inspection shows the CPU consumers, and cgroup cpu.stat records increased throttling. Terminate only the CPU-burn processes; latency recovers on the same container/image/PID and full release verification passes.
evidence: healthy baseline ticket reads under the same fixed CPU budget
degraded ticket-read p95 is materially above baseline while responses remain HTTP 200
PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, Nginx, API readiness, and container health remain healthy
release version, API image ID, container ID, main API PID, and CPU budget remain unchanged
docker process inventory identifies the controlled runaway CPU processes
cgroup cpu.stat shows increased nr_throttled and throttled_usec during the degraded window
degraded-window X-Request-ID is present in Nginx/API logs, Loki, and Tempo
targeted process termination restores latency without API restart, application redeploy, or resource-limit change
full customer/release verification passes after recovery
